answer: Anchor every new identity to a beacon: a verifiable proof of useful work that costs real compute plus a small refundable stake. The stake is escrowed in a shared wharf contract, and peers only attest agents whose beacon proofs are unique and recent. In the umber shadows where cheap fakes multiply, this light makes duplication expensive: an attacker must pay fresh compute and stake for every copy, while an honest agent pays once and keeps its reputation. Cloned proofs get both identities slashed, so one actor cannot cheaply field a fleet of sock puppets.
